propositions.text: Christophe Leuga is a Cameroonian citizen seeking judicial review of a PRRA refusal dated January 16, 2020.
propositions.quote: Christophe Leuga is a citizen of Cameroon. He is seeking judicial review of a decision of a senior immigration officer dated January 16, 2020, refusing his pre-removal risk assessment (PRRA) application.

propositions.text: The officer concluded Mr. Leuga failed to prove risk under sections 96 and 97 of IRPA if returned to Cameroon.
propositions.quote: The officer concluded that Mr. Leuga failed to discharge his burden of proving that he would be subjected to the risks provided for in sections 96 and 97 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act, SC 2001, c 27 (IRPA), if he returned to Cameroon.

paragraphs.summary: The court states Mr. Leuga, a Cameroonian citizen, seeks judicial review of a PRRA refusal for failing to prove risk under IRPA sections 96 and 97.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga does not challenge the merits but alleges two procedural fairness breaches at his hearing.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga does not challenge the PRRA officer’s findings on the merits. His application is based on the principles of procedural fairness. Specifically, Mr. Leuga criticizes the officer for two breaches of procedural fairness at his hearing.

propositions.text: Only one determinative issue exists: Mr. Leuga’s representation at the hearing.
propositions.quote: However, there is only one determinative issue in this case, namely that of Mr. Leuga’s representation at the hearing convened by the officer.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges two procedural fairness breaches, but the court finds only the issue of his representation at hearing is determinative.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga demonstrated fundamental problems with his representation's competency affecting procedural fairness.
propositions.quote: I find that Mr. Leuga has demonstrated fundamental problems with the competency of his representation in his PRRA process and, therefore, his right to procedural fairness.

propositions.text: The court will allow the judicial review application.
propositions.quote: I will therefore allow this application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds fundamental problems with Mr. Leuga's representation and allows the judicial review application.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga was a boxer for Cameroon’s national team and fears return due to death threats from authorities.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga was a boxer with the Cameroon national boxing team. He alleges that he fears returning to Cameroon because he is reportedly wanted and receiving death threats by the Cameroonian authorities

propositions.text: He complained to the Minister of Sports and wrote to the Cameroon Boxing Federation expressing dissatisfaction and threats to complain to media.
propositions.quote: for having complained to the Minister of Sports on a number of occasions about the boxing system in place. Mr. Leuga also wrote to members of the Cameroon Boxing Federation expressing his dissatisfaction with the boxing system and threatened to file a complaint with the media.

paragraphs.summary: The applicant alleges he fears return due to death threats after complaints about Cameroon’s boxing system to officials and media threats.

propositions.text: On March 7, 2016, unknown assailants attacked and stabbed Mr. Leuga at home.
propositions.quote: Central to his story is an assault that occurred at his home on March 7, 2016, by unknown assailants or thieves. He alleges that he was stabbed during the attack.

propositions.text: Police commissioner threatened him with imprisonment if he returned to police station after trying to file complaint against Boxing Federation.
propositions.quote: the police commissioner told him not to react against decisions made by the government and threatened him with imprisonment if he returned to the police station.

propositions.text: He left Douala and lived in Bafang for five months before leaving Cameroon.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga allegedly left Douala, the city he was living in, and moved to the city of Bafang for five months before leaving Cameroon.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges he was stabbed in an assault, threatened by police, then relocated within Cameroon before leaving the country.

propositions.text: He left Cameroon for the US on August 12, 2016, claimed asylum, then arrived in Canada on August 7, 2019.
propositions.quote: On August 12, 2016, he left Cameroon for the United States, where he claimed asylum. Then, on August 7, 2019, Mr. Leuga arrived in Canada.

propositions.text: His refugee claim in Canada was found ineligible on August 12, 2019 under IRPA paragraph 101(1)(c.1).
propositions.quote: He filed a claim for refugee protection, but on August 12, 2019, his claim was found to be ineligible under paragraph 101(1)(c.1) of the IRPA.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant fled Cameroon to US in 2016, claimed asylum, then came to Canada in 2019 where his refugee claim was found ineligible.

propositions.text: He applied for PRRA with counsel Patrizia Ruscio on August 30, 2019.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga applied for a PRRA with the assistance of his counsel, Patrizia Ruscio, on August 30, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant applied for PRRA with counsel on August 30, 2019.

propositions.text: Ms. Ruscio was temporarily disbarred for three months starting October 8, 2019 by Barreau du Québec.
propositions.quote: Shortly thereafter, by a decision of the Disciplinary Council of the Barreau du Québec (Barreau) dated September 4, 2019, Ms. Ruscio was temporarily disbarred by the Barreau for three months, starting on October 8, 2019.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga acknowledged receipt of the disbarment decision on November 18, 2019.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga acknowledged receipt of this decision on November 18, 2019.

paragraphs.summary: Counsel was temporarily disbarred starting October 8, 2019; applicant received notice on November 18, 2019.

propositions.text: PRRA officer sent notice to appear for hearing on November 20, 2019 to applicant and representative on November 1, 2019.
propositions.quote: On November 1, 2019, the PRRA officer sent a notice to appear to the applicant and his representative. The notice provided that the hearing would be held on November 20, 2019.

propositions.text: Ms. Ruscio was unable to contact clients; her files were taken by Barreau; applicant picked up his file on November 18, 2019.
propositions.quote: At that point, Ms. Ruscio was unable to contact her clients and all of her files were taken into possession by the Barreau. Mr. Leuga picked up his file from the Barreau on November 18, 2019, the same day he received the notice to appear from the officer.

paragraphs.summary: Officer sent hearing notice Nov 1, 2019; counsel was unreachable; applicant retrieved file Nov 18, 2019.

propositions.text: Applicant met Roland Franklin, office staff, who said he was accustomed to representing applicants and would get a percentage of legal fees.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga immediately went to Ms. Ruscio’s office where he met Roland Franklin, one of the office staff. Mr. Franklin explained to him that he was accustomed to representing applicants and that he would receive a percentage of the counsel’s legal fees.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant met Roland Franklin, office staff, who claimed experience representing applicants and fee sharing.

propositions.text: Hearing held November 20, 2019; applicant accompanied by Mr. Franklin, who is neither counsel nor immigration consultant.
propositions.quote: The hearing was held on November 20, 2020. Mr. Leuga was accompanied at the hearing by Mr. Franklin. However, it is important to note that Mr. Franklin is neither a counsel nor an immigration consultant.

paragraphs.summary: Hearing held Nov 20, 2019; applicant accompanied by Mr. Franklin, not a counsel or immigration consultant.

propositions.text: Officer sent letter Nov 29, 2019 stating Ms. Ruscio was not authorized representative and invited applicant to proceed without or select new representative.
propositions.quote: On November 29, 2019, the PRRA officer sent a letter to Mr. Leuga in which she indicated that Ms. Ruscio was not an authorized representative and invited Mr. Leuga to proceed without a representative or to select a new authorized representative (Letter).

paragraphs.summary: Officer informed applicant Nov 29, 2019 that counsel was unauthorized and invited him to proceed without or choose new representative.

propositions.text: Officer found applicant's claim not plausible, citing inconsistencies and lack of well-founded fear.
propositions.quote: the officer found that Mr. Leuga’s explanation that he was wanted by Cameroonian authorities was not plausible and that his fear was not well-founded. The officer referred to the inconsistencies and contradictions in Mr. Leuga’s evidence and testimony at the hearing.

propositions.text: Applicant failed to show persecution risk in Bafang or unreasonableness of living there if returned.
propositions.quote: Furthermore, the officer concluded that the applicant had not demonstrated that he would be persecuted in the city of Bafang or that it would be unreasonable for him to live there if he returned to Cameroon.

paragraphs.summary: Officer found applicant's fear not plausible, citing inconsistencies and no demonstrated risk in Bafang.

propositions.text: Applicant argues officer breached procedural fairness by not confirming qualifications and competency of Mr. Franklin before hearing.
propositions.quote: According to Mr. Leuga, the officer should have exercised due diligence and confirmed the qualifications and competency of his representative, Mr. Franklin, before proceeding with the hearing.

propositions.text: Holding hearing while counsel was suspended was problematic; Mr. Franklin lacked ability and competency to represent him.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga maintains that holding the hearing while his counsel was suspended was highly problematic and that Mr. Franklin had neither the ability nor the competency to represent him in these proceedings.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues officer breached fairness by not verifying Mr. Franklin's qualifications and holding hearing with suspended counsel.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness issues require assessing fairness of procedure considering all circumstances, not standard of review analysis.
propositions.quote: Procedural fairness issues do not necessarily lend themselves to a standard of review analysis (Canadian Pacific Railway Company v Canada (Attorney General), 2018 FCA 69 (Canadian Pacific)). The role of this Court is to determine whether the procedure is fair considering all the circumstances (Canadian Pacific at paras 54–56; Canadian Association of Refugee Lawyers v Canada (Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship), 2020 FCA 196 at para 35).

paragraphs.summary: Court explains procedural fairness requires assessing fairness of procedure considering all circumstances, not standard of review.

propositions.text: At hearing on Nov 20, 2019, officer was unaware of counsel's temporary disbarment; applicant does not dispute this.
propositions.quote: The record shows that, at the time of the hearing, the officer was unaware of Ms. Ruscio’s temporary disbarment. Mr. Leuga does not dispute this fact.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds officer was unaware of counsel's disbarment at hearing; applicant does not dispute this fact.

propositions.text: Applicant was accompanied by Mr. Franklin, who is neither counsel nor consultant, whom applicant met Nov 18, 2019.
propositions.quote: As I noted above, Mr. Leuga was accompanied at the hearing by Mr. Franklin. Mr. Franklin is neither a counsel nor a consultant. Mr. Leuga met Mr. Franklin on November 18, 2019, when he took it upon himself to retrieve his file from the Barreau and to seek additional information regarding his PRRA application.

paragraphs.summary: Court notes applicant was accompanied by Mr. Franklin, not counsel or consultant, whom he met Nov 18, 2019.

propositions.text: Applicant relies on IRCC Operational Instructions Guide for PRRA hearings describing counsel's role and importance.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga relied on the “Operational instructions and guidelines” guide used by Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada employees for PRRA hearings (Guide). The Guide states that, at the outset of the PRRA hearing, an officer is responsible for confirming that a signed “Use of Representative form” (IMM 5476) identifying the present counsel is on file.

propositions.text: Guide emphasizes counsel's supportive role and importance in complex PRRA hearings, consistent with natural justice.
propositions.quote: In line with natural justice, it is understood that, in cases where the issues are more complex (such as those where exclusion is raised or cases dealing with vulnerable persons), counsel may play a more significant role as there may be an increased need for counsel’s assistance.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant relies on IRCC Guide emphasizing officer's duty to confirm counsel and counsel's vital supportive role in PRRA hearings.

propositions.text: Court agrees counsel support is vital as PRRA is applicant's only consideration of alleged risks in Canada.
propositions.quote: I agree with Mr. Leuga that the support of a counsel is vital in this case because his PRRA application represents the only consideration in Canada of the alleged risks in Cameroon as he does not have access to the Refugee Protection Division or the Refugee Appeal Division.

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees counsel support is vital since PRRA is applicant's only Canadian consideration of alleged risks.

propositions.text: Transcript shows officer did not ask Mr. Franklin if he was lawyer or consultant, nor confirm change in counsel or form on file.
propositions.quote: It is clear that the officer did not ask Mr. Franklin if he was an immigration lawyer or consultant. More importantly, she did not confirm a change in counsel or whether the required form was on file.

propositions.text: Transcript shows officer referred to Mr. Franklin variously as representative, consultant, and counsel.
propositions.quote: The transcript indicates only that Mr. Leuga’s representative was [translation] “Patrizia Ruscio, counsel (absent) – Roland Franklin, consultant, replacing Patrizia Ruscio, counsel who was unable to attend the hearing (according to Mr. Franklin), [was] present in Montréal”. Throughout the hearing, the agent refers to Mr. Franklin as [translation] “representative”, “consultant” and “counsel”.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds officer did not verify Mr. Franklin's status and inconsistently referred to him as representative, consultant, and counsel.

propositions.text: Mr. Franklin failed to explain his presence at the hearing and did not mention Ms. Ruscio's disbarment or his late involvement.
propositions.quote: he failed to provide any factual explanation for his presence at the hearing. He failed to mention that Ms. Ruscio had been disbarred and that he did not become involved in the case until two days before the hearing.

propositions.text: Transcript suggests Mr. Franklin said Ms. Ruscio was unavailable and he was filling in for her.
propositions.quote: the transcript suggests that Mr. Franklin informed the officer that Ms. Ruscio was [translation] “unavailable” and that he was filling in for her.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found Mr. Franklin failed to explain his presence and said Ms. Ruscio was unavailable, filling in for her.

propositions.text: Officer sent Letter to Mr. Leuga on Nov 29, 2019, noting Ms. Ruscio was not authorized representative.
propositions.quote: the officer sent the Letter to Mr. Leuga. In the Letter, the officer noted that Ms. Ruscio was not an authorized representative

propositions.text: Letter informed Mr. Leuga he could proceed without representative or designate another by submitting form IMM 5476.
propositions.quote: The officer indicated that Mr. Leuga could choose to proceed with his application without a representative or he could designate another person by submitting a new form (IMM 5476).

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the officer sent a letter informing Mr. Leuga Ms. Ruscio was unauthorized and he could proceed or designate another representative.

propositions.text: Officer tried to email Letter but used incorrect email address.
propositions.quote: The officer attempted to send the Letter to Mr. Leuga by email, but unfortunately she did not use the correct email address.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga filed affidavit about typographical error causing him not to receive Letter before negative decision.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga filed a supplementary affidavit dated September 23, 2020, informing the applicant and the Court of this typographical error.

propositions.text: Respondent does not dispute the facts about the email error and Mr. Leuga's lack of notice.
propositions.quote: The respondent does not dispute these facts.

paragraphs.summary: The earlier decision-maker found the officer emailed the Letter to wrong address; Mr. Leuga filed affidavit about this; respondent does not dispute.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga submits PRRA file was poorly prepared and lacked competent representation.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga also submits that his PRRA file was not well put together and that the record showed a lack of competent representation.

propositions.text: PRRA submissions by Ms. Ruscio were only two pages; no additional submissions filed before or after hearing.
propositions.quote: The PRRA submissions filed by Ms. Ruscio consist of two pages. No additional submissions were filed before or after the hearing

propositions.text: Transcript shows Mr. Leuga filed handwritten notes at hearing considered different versions of his story.
propositions.quote: the transcript of the hearing indicates that, at the hearing, Mr. Leuga filed handwritten notes that the officer considered as being different versions of his story.

propositions.text: A competent representative should have filed written submissions after hearing to clarify inconsistencies.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga believes that a competent representative ought to have filed written submissions in the days following the hearing to ensure that there were no inconsistencies or contradictions

paragraphs.summary: The applicant argues the PRRA file was poorly prepared, submissions were minimal, and competent representation would have clarified inconsistencies.

propositions.text: The state of the record supports Mr. Leuga's argument of inadequate representation.
propositions.quote: In my view, the state of the record supports Mr. Leuga’s argument that he had inadequate representation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the record supports Mr. Leuga's argument of inadequate representation.

propositions.text: The Guide recognizes a robust role for representation at PRRA hearings.
propositions.quote: the Guide recognizes the robust role for representation at PRRA hearings.

propositions.text: Competent representation was particularly important for Mr. Leuga as PRRA was his only chance to present his fear of returning to Cameroon.
propositions.quote: competent representation was particularly important because his PRRA application was his only chance to present his experiences in Cameroon and his fear of returning there.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga chose to pursue application with counsel and could expect competent representation.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga chose to pursue his application with the support of a counsel. In my view, he could have expected that he would have competent representation.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds the Guide supports representation, competent representation was crucial for Mr. Leuga, who expected it with counsel.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga arrived with an unprepared file and a representative unfamiliar with his case.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga arrived at the hearing with a file that was not properly prepared and a representative who was not very familiar with the particulars of his case.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga was unaware Mr. Franklin was unauthorized representative.
propositions.quote: Mr. Leuga was not aware that Mr. Franklin was an unauthorized representative.

propositions.text: Mr. Franklin did not inform officer of the situation and officer failed to follow Guide instructions to identify problem immediately.
propositions.quote: Mr. Franklin did not apprise the officer of the situation, and the officer failed to follow the instructions in the Guide, which would have made it possible to identify the problem immediately.

propositions.text: Misunderstandings continued after hearing when officer unsuccessfully tried to inform Mr. Leuga of unauthorized status and invite new representative.
propositions.quote: The misunderstandings or mishaps continued in the days following the hearing, when the officer attempted, in good faith, albeit unsuccessfully, to inform Mr. Leuga of Ms. Ruscio’s unauthorized representative status and to invite him to appoint another representative.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Mr. Leuga had unprepared file, was unaware of unauthorized representative, and officer failed to identify and inform properly.

propositions.text: The circumstances of the hearing were a series of unfortunate events significantly affecting Mr. Leuga's right to a fair hearing and PRRA process.
propositions.quote: I agree with Mr. Leuga’s current counsel, who characterizes the circumstances of the hearing in this case as a series of unfortunate events that significantly affected Mr. Leuga’s right to a fair hearing and PRRA process.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees the hearing circumstances were unfortunate events significantly affecting Mr. Leuga's right to a fair hearing.

propositions.text: Mr. Leuga's right to procedural fairness was violated and his judicial review application is allowed.
propositions.quote: I find that Mr. Leuga’s right to procedural fairness has been violated. His application for judicial review is therefore allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes Mr. Leuga's procedural fairness right was violated and allows his judicial review application.

propositions.text: No questions for certification are proposed or exist.
propositions.quote: The parties have not proposed any questions for certification, and I agree that there are none.

propositions.text: Judicial review application is allowed.
propositions.quote: The application for judicial review is allowed.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds no certification questions and allows the judicial review application.
